basis: Cash basis, continuing operations, Group net interest margin (as reported, not statutory). FY25 comparator is the same as CBA's own FY25 profit announcement disclosure (2.08%, cash, continuing operations) and is not restated in the FY26 accounts.

movement.unit: bps (endpoints shown in %, delta and driver contributions in bps)

headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 3bps, from 2.08% in FY25 to 2.05% in FY26. The whole of the decline is attributed by CBA to the dilutive mix effect of growth in lower-margin liquid assets; the other named drivers in CBA's own NIM walk net to zero, so CBA describes underlying margin (ex-liquids) as 'broadly stable' / 'stable'.

drivers.name: Liquids (mix effect of growth in average liquid assets)
drivers.narrative: Average liquid assets grew $15bn (9%) YoY to $187bn. This dollar income is broadly neutral to net interest income but dilutes the ratio because liquids carry lower margins than lending assets. CBA states that excluding this liquids mix effect, NIM was stable. The results presentation shows a combined 'Liquids & repos' bar of -4bps, footnoted as -3bps from liquid assets and -1bp from institutional repos; the profit announcement isolates the liquids-only effect at -3bps and places the repo effect inside 'Treasury and Markets' instead (see disagreements).

citations.quote: Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin was stable.
Liquid asset average balances increased $15 billion or 9% on the prior year to $187 billion.
(0.03%) [chart data label positioned directly under the 'Liquids' bar in the FY26 NIM walk chart, Jun25-to-Jun26 full year]
+$15bn increase in average liquid assets and +$11bn increase in average institutional repos in FY26 vs FY25.
Increase in liquid assets (3)
Every additional $10bn of liquid assets is expected to reduce Group NIM by ~2bpts
Margins were broadly stable excluding growth in liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income.

drivers.name: Asset pricing (lending competition)
drivers.narrative: Home lending pricing cut margin by 4bps and business/institutional lending pricing cut margin by a further 1bp, both attributed to competitive pressure. This is the largest single negative driver and is quantified identically (-5bps total) in both the profit announcement text and the results-presentation chart; the presentation further splits the -4bps home lending figure into -3bps competition and -1bp cash rate lag, which reconciles exactly (-3-1=-4) rather than conflicting.

citations.quote: Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 5 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 4 basis points) and business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point), primarily reflecting the impact of competition.

drivers.name: Funding costs
drivers.narrative: CBA reports this driver as 'Flat', i.e. no material net contribution to the FY26-vs-FY25 movement. This is a quantified zero, not an unmeasured driver.

drivers.name: Portfolio mix (asset and funding mix)
drivers.narrative: Favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending, and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits, added 2bps. Quantified identically in both CBA documents.

citations.quote: Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by favourable asset mix from strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits.
Favourable asset mix and deposits growing faster than lending

drivers.name: Basis risk
drivers.narrative: CBA reports this driver as 'Flat' in the profit announcement's seven-bucket walk. The results presentation's six-bucket walk does not show a separate basis-risk line, consistent with an immaterial (zero) value, but this is not independently confirmed as a distinct line in that document.

citations.quote: Basis risk: Flat.

drivers.name: Capital, replicating portfolio and other (interest rate risk hedging)
drivers.narrative: Higher earnings on the replicating portfolio (+4bps, from changes in portfolio rate and volume as swap rates rose) plus higher earnings on capital hedges (+1bp). Labelled 'Capital, Replicating and Other' in the profit announcement and 'Interest rate risk hedging' in the results presentation; both give the identical +5bps split as +4bps / +1bp.

citations.quote: Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 5 basis points driven by higher earnings on the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).

drivers.name: Treasury and Markets
drivers.narrative: Lower risk management income in Treasury, plus growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances, cut margin by 2bps in the profit announcement's walk. The results presentation instead shows 'Treasury & Markets' as only -1bp, because it moves the repo-balance effect (-1bp) into its combined 'Liquids & repos' bucket. See disagreements.

citations.quote: Treasury and Markets: Decreased margin by 2 basis points due to lower risk management income in Treasury and growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.
Increase in institutional repos (1)

residual_note: The seven quantified drivers above sum to exactly -3bps (-3 -5 +0 +2 +0 +5 -2 = -3), matching the reported movement with no unexplained residual.

disagreements.topic: Split of the liquids / institutional repo / Treasury effect between the profit announcement's 7-bucket NIM walk and the results presentation's 6-bucket NIM walk
values: Profit announcement (PDF p.28-29): Liquids -3bps; Funding costs 0bps; Basis risk 0bps; Treasury and Markets -2bps
Results presentation (PDF p.60): Liquids & repos -4bps (footnoted as -3bps liquid assets + -1bp institutional repos); Funding costs 0bps; no separate Basis risk line; Treasury & Markets -1bp
disagreements.preferred: Profit announcement breakdown: Liquids -3bps, Treasury and Markets -2bps, Basis risk 0bps
disagreements.explanation: Both walks total the same -3bps and agree exactly on Asset pricing (-5bps), Portfolio mix (+2bps), and the replicating-portfolio/capital-hedge bucket (+5bps). They diverge only in how a combined -4bps liquids-and-repo effect is allocated: the presentation nets liquid assets (-3bps) and institutional repos (-1bp) into one 'Liquids & repos' bar and shows a smaller residual 'Treasury & Markets' (-1bp); the profit announcement keeps 'Liquids' pure at -3bps and folds the repo effect into its 'Treasury and Markets' figure (-2bps total). The profit announcement is preferred because it is the primary, more granular disclosure (seven named buckets vs. six) with narrative text that explicitly names both causes of the -2bps Treasury and Markets figure, and its numbers reconcile arithmetically to the presentation's split once the repo effect is reallocated.

limitations: The Liquids, Funding costs, and Basis risk bar values on the profit announcement's NIM walk chart (PDF p.28) were read as text data-labels aligned to category labels by horizontal (x-axis) position, because the chart's underlying text layer does not print them in reading order. The mapping was cross-checked by confirming the seven bucket values sum exactly to the disclosed -3bps total, and by confirming the results-presentation's independent chart reconciles to the same total.

CBA's own bucket boundaries for the liquids/repo/Treasury/basis-risk effects differ between the profit announcement and the results presentation (see disagreements); the driver-level figures used here follow the profit announcement's more granular seven-bucket version.

Divisional NIM movements disclosed in the profit announcement (Retail Banking Services -1bp to 2.50%, Business Banking +7bps to 3.39%, Institutional Banking and Markets -6bps to 0.87%, New Zealand/ASB +3bps to 2.30%, all PDF p.20) were not separately reconciled to the seven group-level driver bps above; they are directional corroboration only, not additional quantified drivers.

A bank-defined 'underlying NIM' (ex-liquids and ex-repos) of 2.04% (FY25, rebased) to 2.05% (FY26), i.e. +1bp, is disclosed in the results presentation (PDF p.6, footnoted on p.130). This is consistent with the -3bps headline move less the -4bps liquids-and-repos effect, but was not used here as an independent driver to avoid double-counting.
CBA-FY26-items-impacting-note.pdf is present in the same source folder but was not in the approved source list for this task and was not used.

All figures are CBA's own cash-basis, continuing-operations Group NIM; no independent recalculation of NIM from underlying net interest income and average interest earning assets was performed beyond the cross-check that 25,586 / 1,245,684 and 24,023 / 1,153,684 are consistent in direction with the reported 2.05% and 2.08% (exact NIM calculation methodology, e.g. day-count and averaging convention, is not disclosed in enough detail to replicate to the basis point).
